Capability / Principle: Integrated filtered-water + normal-water faucet. Integrates drinking-water outlet into a normal pull-down kitchen faucet using a separate filter path and solenoid control. Pressing the electric button commands a solenoid box to open the drinking-water path; normal tap water remains separately controllable.
Maturity: Source describes patented technology but does not independently verify patent scope or performance; electrical components add complexity.
Key Constraints: Combines filtered and normal water in one faucet footprint and avoids a second dedicated filter faucet.

Capability / Principle: Fine-particle spray for soaking/cleaning. Uses a dedicated spray outlet geometry to generate fine water particles for soaking food, dishes and kitchenware. Water is divided through fine outlets to form a micro-particle spray.
Maturity: Supplier material does not provide independent cleaning-performance test data.
Key Constraints: Provides a different cleaning/wetting mode from conventional aerated or rinse spray.

Capability / Principle: Aerated + rinse + Na-Micro spray switching. One spray head combines three water functions. Internal flow path switches among aerated, rinse and Na-Micro outlets.
Maturity: More flow paths and components increase design/cleaning complexity.
Key Constraints: Multiple task-oriented spray modes in one compact head.

Capability / Principle: Low-effort mechanical spray selection. A pull switch selects aerated or rinse spray and returns to the default mode when water is turned off. A 4 mm mechanical stroke changes the active spray path; spring/self-reset behavior restores the default.
Maturity: Supplier evidence is product proposal-level; durability data not provided.
Key Constraints: Reduces button interaction and prevents the user from leaving the faucet in the alternate spray mode.

Capability / Principle: Hands-free faucet activation. Uses a low-power laser induction sensor with a solenoid valve. Sensor detects hand/object presence and commands the solenoid to open water.
Maturity: Sensor/solenoid system adds electronics and power requirements; response/reliability data not provided.
Key Constraints: Hands-free operation with a compact sensor concept.

Capability / Principle: Filtered shower water using KDF media. Runner proposal uses a KDF filter element integrated into a shower set. Water passes through a replaceable KDF media element before reaching the shower outlet.
Maturity: Filter life, contaminant-removal performance and pressure loss require verification.
Key Constraints: Adds filtration to a shower without requiring a separate external filter unit.

Capability / Principle: Reduce post-use dripping from shower. Shower set incorporates a quick drip-stop structure. Internal hydraulic geometry/valving is intended to stop residual water after shutoff.
Maturity: Mechanism and long-term effectiveness are not detailed in the source.
Key Constraints: Targets nuisance dripping without requiring user action.

Capability / Principle: Change shower function through replaceable outlet module. Shower concept uses interchangeable outlet parts to provide different spray combinations. The outlet module defines the active spray geometry/function and can be exchanged for another configuration.
Maturity: Requires mechanical compatibility and sealing; changing modules is not necessarily a consumer-friendly interaction.
Key Constraints: Allows one platform to support flushing, private-care and massage-oriented spray configurations.

Capability / Principle: Slim concealed thermostatic shower architecture. Uses a concealed cartridge and slimmer thermostatic construction to reduce built-in depth. Cartridge and control architecture are packaged inside a shallow concealed body.
Maturity: Exact thermal-performance mechanism is not disclosed; installation tolerance remains a constraint.
Key Constraints: Enables slimmer concealed shower design and potential cost reduction.

Capability / Principle: Hydraulic outlet switching without electronic control. A hydraulic switch is proposed to switch between showerhead and hand shower. Water pressure/flow activates an internal hydraulic switching mechanism when the control is operated.
Maturity: Hydraulic behavior depends on pressure/flow conditions; detailed switching mechanism and reliability need verification.
Key Constraints: Can route shower functions without adding electronic control.

Capability / Principle: Non-metallic inner waterway for shower/faucet. Uses a PPA plastic waterway inside a metal housing. Molded polymer waterway carries water while the outer housing provides structure/appearance.
Maturity: Material compatibility, certification, aging and thermal performance must be verified for target application.
Key Constraints: Reduces processing complexity, supports diversified exterior designs and avoids lead contribution from brass waterway.

Capability / Principle: Push-button on/off or function control cartridge. Ceramic/mechanical cartridge operated by a push button for shower/faucet control. Axial button movement actuates the cartridge to open/close or change a function.
Maturity: Exact internal mechanism and endurance depend on model; source catalog does not establish user-level differentiation.
Key Constraints: Allows compact front-facing control and separates button interaction from conventional lever operation.

Capability / Principle: Push-button temperature-control cartridge. Hent catalog includes a button-controlled ceramic cartridge for temperature adjustment. Button/rotary interface actuates the ceramic control elements to regulate temperature.
Maturity: Detailed temperature-control behavior and safety performance require model-specific verification.
Key Constraints: Compact control architecture suitable for concealed shower interfaces.

Capability / Principle: Thermostatic mixing cartridge. Thermostatic cartridges regulate mixed-water temperature using a temperature-responsive control element. The cartridge changes hot/cold mixing ratio in response to outlet temperature.
Maturity: Performance, response time and anti-scald behavior are model-dependent; supplier catalog alone is not proof of superiority.
Key Constraints: Provides stable temperature control in compact cartridge form.

Capability / Principle: Faucet waterway construction options for brass/zinc bodies. Hent provides waterway configurations for different faucet body materials and structures. Internal water path is designed to suit brass or zinc faucet construction and cartridge geometry.
Maturity: Source focuses on structure/catalog coverage rather than quantified user benefit.
Key Constraints: Supports multiple body architectures and manufacturing configurations.

Capability / Principle: Shower column / hand shower with integrated filter. Lota proposes a filter integrated into the shower column or hand shower. Water passes through an internal filter element within the shower product.
Maturity: Filter capacity, pressure loss, replacement method and filtration performance need verification.
Key Constraints: Integrates filtration into the shower form factor rather than using an external filter.

Capability / Principle: Magnetic hand-spray docking. Uses magnetic docking to locate and retain a spray head. Magnet provides self-alignment and holding force when the spray head approaches the dock.
Maturity: Magnetic force, long-term retention and geometry constraints need verification.
Key Constraints: Fast, intuitive docking with potential one-handed operation.

Capability / Principle: Rotatable spout for directional personal washing. A 90-degree spout rotation switches between upward facial spray and downward hair/body washing. Rotating the spout changes the water outlet direction/function.
Maturity: Directional ergonomics and splash control require validation.
Key Constraints: Uses the faucet body itself as a multi-purpose personal-care interface without a separate hand shower.

Capability / Principle: Dedicated low-pressure cleaning spray. A button activates a powerful fan-shaped cleaning spray; source positions it for cleaning the spray face. Internal spray path creates a fan-shaped high-force jet for debris removal.
Maturity: Cleaning effectiveness and ability to remove mineral scale rather than loose debris need verification.
Key Constraints: Integrates a self-cleaning/cleaning function into the spray head.

Capability / Principle: Pressure-responsive spray behavior. Nozzle changes spray force as inlet pressure increases. Internal nozzle geometry reacts to pressure so spray force changes with pressure condition.
Maturity: Mechanism and control range are not fully disclosed; performance claims need testing.
Key Constraints: Potentially broadens usable spray behavior across different water-pressure conditions.

Capability / Principle: On-demand higher-flow spray. Default eco spray is used for daily operation; pressing a button provides a stronger burst and then auto-resets. A button changes the flow/spray path to a higher-flow mode and returns to eco mode automatically.
Maturity: Actual flow increase, pressure requirement and water-saving impact require verification.
Key Constraints: Combines low-flow daily use with an on-demand strong spray without requiring a permanently high flow setting.

Capability / Principle: Standardized modular inner-waterway platform. Uses flexible PERT tubing and standardized connections for top-control and side-control faucets. Modular non-metallic waterway sections connect through standardized interfaces and route mixed water internally.
Maturity: Certification, long-term durability, thermal/pressure performance and serviceability require application-specific verification.
Key Constraints: Reduces platform/tooling investment and can accelerate multiple faucet designs.

Capability / Principle: Long-life silent high-flow cartridge. 35 mm cartridge family combines long-life ceramic design, low noise and high flow capability. Ceramic control elements regulate flow/temperature with a design optimized for durability and reduced chatter.
Maturity: High-flow performance is pressure-dependent; superiority over competing cartridges needs standardized benchmark data.
Key Constraints: Offers a combination of high flow and long endurance for shower/bath applications.

Capability / Principle: Mid-way lever stop for water saving. Lever has a mid-way stop at approximately 60% of stroke to reduce water flow during normal use. Mechanical stop limits the lever position until the user deliberately moves beyond it.
Maturity: Actual water saving depends on user behavior and downstream hydraulic design.
Key Constraints: Can encourage lower flow without electronics or a separate user control.

Capability / Principle: Cold-start energy saving. Cartridge architecture centers cold water in the normal lever-start position so hot water is not drawn unintentionally. Internal port geometry keeps hot-water path closed until the lever is moved toward hot.
Maturity: Energy benefit depends on user behavior and hot-water system layout.
Key Constraints: Reduces unnecessary hot-water demand with a passive mechanical interface.

Capability / Principle: Extended-durability surface/ceramic technology. Sedal describes Nano Shelter as extending cartridge durability. A nano-scale surface/material treatment is used on cartridge components to reduce wear/friction.
Maturity: Detailed material chemistry and independent comparative endurance evidence are not provided.
Key Constraints: Potential for longer service life without changing user interaction.

Capability / Principle: Short-height thermostatic cartridge. Compact thermostatic cartridge reduces height by approximately 15% versus a reference design. Thermostatic sensing/mixing elements are packaged into a shorter cartridge body.
Maturity: Exact response/safety performance and installation envelope need verification.
Key Constraints: Enables slimmer concealed shower architecture and more compact valve packaging.

Capability / Principle: Thermostatic cartridge optimized for low-pressure/high-flow use. Sedal presents a thermostatic configuration delivering high flow under low-pressure conditions. Thermostatic cartridge and flow path are tuned to preserve flow at lower inlet pressure.
Maturity: Flow figures are supplier test data; target installation conditions and independent validation are required.
Key Constraints: Directly relevant to low-pressure shower performance while retaining thermostatic control.

Capability / Principle: Slim concealed thermostatic shower control. Solex uses a slimmer thermostatic cartridge and concealed architecture for reduced built-in depth. Cartridge and control mechanism are packaged into a shallow concealed cassette.
Maturity: Detailed thermal response and serviceability are not fully disclosed.
Key Constraints: Supports slim wall architecture and potential cost advantage.

Capability / Principle: Integrated service shut-off in concealed shower body. Main body includes a water shut-off valve below the cassette. A built-in valve isolates water at the product for service or installation.
Maturity: Adds internal components and requires reliable sealing over product life.
Key Constraints: Can simplify service isolation without relying only on upstream building valves.

Capability / Principle: Protect internal waterways during construction. Protective structure prevents construction soil entering waterways and allows waterway leak testing before final use. Temporary/protective interfaces isolate the waterway and enable pressure/leak verification.
Maturity: Primarily an installation feature rather than a direct end-user experience innovation.
Key Constraints: Addresses construction contamination and installation-quality risk in concealed shower systems.

Capability / Principle: Passive water-hammer absorption. An airbag structure is used to absorb pressure fluctuations caused by rapid flow changes. Compressible air volume cushions pressure spikes in the closed piping system.
Maturity: Sizing, durability and effectiveness depend on hydraulic system conditions.
Key Constraints: Potentially reduces noise, vibration and cartridge damage without electronic control.

Capability / Principle: High-endurance push-button cartridge. Solex states its push-button cartridge reaches 500,000 cycles versus a stated 200,000-cycle standard. Ceramic/mechanical cartridge uses a push-button interface with an endurance-oriented design.
Maturity: Cycle figure is supplier claim and requires standardized test evidence before using it as a performance benchmark.
Key Constraints: Combines compact push control with a high stated cycle life.

Capability / Principle: Pressure-adaptive spray-hole architecture. Spray nozzle hole diameter/arrangement is varied to produce stronger spray at low pressure and balanced pressure at higher pressure. Small outlet geometry increases jet force at low pressure; larger/adjusted outlet geometry balances spray at high pressure.
Maturity: Source provides comparative force data but exact fluid mechanism and independent validation require further testing.
Key Constraints: Targets consistent shower sensation across a wider pressure range.

Capability / Principle: Targeted T-shaped massage spray. T-shaped spray pattern concentrates jet force on shoulder/spine regions with a stated coverage above 200 mm. Outlet geometry creates a T-shaped high-force spray region.
Maturity: Massage benefit is subjective; ergonomics, pressure requirement and safety need validation.
Key Constraints: Moves from generic massage to targeted body-area coverage.

Capability / Principle: Height-adjustable overhead shower with reduced wobble. Mechanical support system allows approximately 300 mm height adjustment and is designed to reduce wobble under water load. Counteracting/optimized support geometry changes the balance of forces during adjustment and water flow.
Maturity: Force balance is installation-dependent; durability data are supplier test claims.
Key Constraints: Combines family height adjustment with improved stability during use.

Capability / Principle: Reverse-flushing shower spray face. Spray panel can be reversed to flush impurities from the opposite side and can be removed for cleaning/replacement. Reversing the outlet panel changes the flow direction through the outlet passages; removable panel permits manual cleaning.
Maturity: Does not prevent scale elsewhere in the hydraulic path; reverse-flush effectiveness needs testing.
Key Constraints: Addresses clogging at the spray face without replacing the whole shower head.

Capability / Principle: Interchangeable spray panels for different pressure ranges. Supplier offers panels intended for low, middle and high water-pressure areas. Different outlet-hole configurations tune spray behavior to pressure/flow conditions.
Maturity: Requires panel selection or supply-chain complexity; users may not know their pressure condition.
Key Constraints: Potentially improves shower experience across regional pressure differences without changing the whole head.

Capability / Principle: Dual spray architecture for personal care and massage. Combines dense/soft spray with granular particle spray or pressurizing spray. Different outlet groups create separate spray sensations in one shower head.
Maturity: Multiple outlet groups increase hydraulic/design complexity; source does not independently validate skin-care benefits.
Key Constraints: Combines cleansing, personal-care and massage use cases in one platform.

Capability / Principle: On-demand ozone-treated water. Ozone water is generated/dispensed through a dedicated activation system and can be operated touchlessly. Ozone generation is coupled to the water outlet; side sensor can activate the system.
Maturity: Ozone concentration, contact time, residual control, safety and certification are critical verification items; supplier claims are not treated as validated performance.
Key Constraints: Introduces a water-treatment function at point of use rather than relying on soap/chemical cleaning.

Capability / Principle: Visual feedback linked to water-flow adjustment. LED light intensity changes in synchronization with flow-rate adjustment. Electronic control maps flow setting to dynamic light feedback.
Maturity: Adds electronics and has limited direct functional benefit unless feedback improves control or accessibility.
Key Constraints: Makes flow adjustment visually legible and adds an interaction cue without relying on a screen.

Capability / Principle: Automatic shut-off after a preset water volume. Faucet automatically stops after a specified volume, with examples such as filling a pot or sink. Electronic control tracks dispensed volume and closes the water valve at the target quantity.
Maturity: Requires flow measurement/control accuracy and power; source does not provide accuracy or fail-safe data.
Key Constraints: Hands-free measured dispensing can reduce overflow and repetitive monitoring.

Capability / Principle: Touch/display shower controller with user presets. Touch interface controls temperature, flow, function and user modes while display shows temperature, flow and shower timing. Electronic controller communicates with shower control hardware and stores user presets.
Maturity: Higher electrical/system complexity; reliability and user-value versus simpler controls require validation.
Key Constraints: Combines personalized control with direct temperature/flow feedback and pre-drainage of cold water.

Capability / Principle: Push-button diverter for shower outlet selection. Yizhan catalog includes push-button diverter cartridges, including versions with flow adjustment. Button actuation changes the active outlet; variants combine diverter and flow adjustment.
Maturity: Internal mechanism and durability are model-dependent; catalog does not establish differentiation versus competitors.
Key Constraints: Compact multi-function control suitable for concealed shower interfaces.

Capability / Principle: Push-button hot/cold temperature control. Cartridge combines push-button operation with hot/cold temperature adjustment. Button and rotary/ceramic elements control opening and temperature mixing.
Maturity: Exact user interface and safety behavior require model-specific validation.
Key Constraints: Combines on/off and temperature functions in one compact control architecture.

Capability / Principle: Two-phase cold-start water-saving cartridge. Yizhan offers cold-start variants in 35/40 mm cartridge families. Lever starts from a cold-water position and accesses hot water only after intentional movement.
Maturity: Energy benefit depends on user behavior and plumbing layout.
Key Constraints: Passive mechanical reduction of unintended hot-water draw.

Capability / Principle: Two-phase flow-control cartridge. Yizhan presents large-flow and small-flow two-phase cartridge variants. Lever positions provide distinct flow-rate stages rather than continuously exposing maximum flow.
Maturity: User behavior and downstream pressure determine actual water savings.
Key Constraints: Can give a low-flow default while retaining a higher-flow option.

Capability / Principle: Reduce heat transfer to external faucet surfaces. Yizhan materials present cool-touch architecture together with thermostatic/shower faucet cartridge solutions. Thermal path/material/structural separation reduces heat transferred to the user-touch surface.
Maturity: Mechanism is not sufficiently detailed in catalog; requires thermal test data.
Key Constraints: Adds contact-surface thermal safety beyond water-temperature regulation.
